editorial:
Imagine you are just trying to finish your work shift at a space warehouse when a coworker shows up looking totally wasted. That is how things kick off here. You get a small cast of characters and a very gritty, industrial feel that makes you feel like you are right there in the grime of a space colony. The vibe is tense from the start, making you wonder if the trucker is actually drunk or if something much scarier is going on. It feels like a love letter to the original space horror movies, keeping things small and focused while building up a lot of dread.

What really works here is how the movie builds tension without needing a huge budget. The acting is believable, and the pacing keeps you on your toes until the big reveal. One downside is that it is very short, so you might want more story, but it hits hard while it lasts. If you love creature features, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The twist reveals that the trucker isn't drunk at all. He has a chestburster alien inside him. As the movie reaches its peak, the creature rips through his chest in a bloody mess. The young worker tries to survive the attack, but the alien is too fast and strong. In the end, the creature wins, leaving the warehouse a crime scene. It is a quick, brutal finish that proves you can never trust a strange coworker.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves short horror stories and Alien movies.
